algorithm.title: Algorithm for the Management of Patients with OCD.

cell.label: First-line treatment options: cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), SSRI, or both.
cell.path: SSRIs, or both CBT and SSRIs

cell.label: Is the response adequate after 13 to 20 weekly sessions of CBT?
For medication continue for 1 to 2 years, then consider gradual taper over several months or more. For CBT: provide periodic booster sessions for 3 to 6 months after acute treatment.
Is the response adequate after 8 to 12 total weeks of SSRI (4–6 weeks at maximal tolerable dose) or 13 to 20 weekly sessions of CBT or weekday daily CBT for 3 weeks?

Strategies for Moderate Response: Augment with a second-generation antipsychotic or with CBT (ERP) if not already provided; or add cognitive therapy to ERP.* Strategies for little or no response: Switch to a difference SSRI (may try more than one trial); switch to clomipramine; augment with a second-generation antipsychotic; switch to venlafaxine; switch to mirtazapine.*

Strategies for moderate and for little or no response: switch to a different augmenting second-generation antipsychotic; switch to a different SRI; augment with clomipramine; * augment with buspirone, * pindolol, * morphine sulfate, * inositol, * or a glutamate antagonist ( eg, riluzole, topiramate). * Strategies only for little or no response: switch to D–amphetamine monotherapy; * switch to tramadol monotherapy; * switch to ondansetron monotherapy; * switch to an MAOI. * After first - and second-line strategies have been exhausted, other options that may be considered include transcranial magnetic stimulation, * deep brain stimulation, * and ablative neurosurgery.

footnotes.footnote: From Koran LM, Hanna GL, Hollander E, et al. Practice guideline for the treatment of patients with obsessive-compulsive disorder. Am J Psychiatry 2007;164:5-53.
